s0.chart.text: Here is a stock that has gone up a long way over the past six months. [[0.35]] Nothing unusual about that. There are always some.

s0.two.text: Two people look at exactly this chart and say opposite things. [[0.45]] It has run too far, it will come back. [[0.4]] It is moving, it will keep moving.

s0.real.text: These are not moods. They are both real strategies with real money behind them, and each one has years where it is the only thing working.

s0.question.text: So. [[0.5]] The same chart, two opposite bets. What decides which one is right?

s1.measure.text: The honest way to settle that is to stop arguing and measure it. [[0.35]] One chart proves nothing, so take the whole market.

s1.cross.text: Two hundred and forty stocks, two hundred and fifty years. [[0.35]] This is a simulated market, and later that will matter twice.

s1.signal.text: For each stock, one number. What it did over the last six months. [[0.3]] Today's price, over the price six months ago, minus one.

s1.rank.text: Now sort the entire market by that number. [[0.45]] Buy the strongest tenth. Short the weakest tenth.

s1.rule.text: Wait a while, and then do it again. [[0.4]] That is the whole rule. There is nothing else in it.

s1.result.text: And over two hundred and fifty years of this market, it makes one point zero nine percent a month. [[0.5]] Momentum wins.

s1.change.text: Except. [[0.45]] Change one number. Not the market. Not the rule. [[0.35]] The six.

s1.one.text: Rank on the last month instead of the last six months. Same code, same market, same day. [[0.4]] Minus zero point five five.

s1.four.text: Rank on the last four years. [[0.45]] Minus zero point one zero.

s1.lesson.text: So, does momentum work, was never a question about the market. [[0.4]] It is a question about a number we picked without thinking.

s2.second.text: And there is a second number hidden in, do it again. [[0.4]] How long do you hold, before you re-sort?

s2.hold.text: Hold that same six-month signal for one month and it pays one point zero nine. Hold it two years and it pays six hundredths. [[0.35]] Same signal.

s2.pair.text: So a strategy is not a rule. [[0.45]] It is a pair of numbers. And every pair is a different strategy.

s2.floor.text: Lookback along one axis, holding period along the other. [[0.3]] Each step doubles the months.

s2.dot.text: And everything we just built, all of it, [[0.35]] is one dot on this floor.

s2.all.text: So run all of them. [[0.4]] Forty-eight lookbacks, by twenty-four holding periods. Eleven hundred and fifty-two complete backtests.

s2.height.text: Every one of them has a number attached. What it paid. [[0.45]] Give each dot that number, as its height.

s2.nothing.text: [[0.4]] Nothing happened. [[0.7]] Every dot just moved, and from straight above you cannot see any of it. [[0.4]] Height is the one direction this view does not have.

s3.landscape.text: They were all sitting at their own heights the whole time. [[0.5]] It is a landscape.

s3.ridge.text: Up here, ranking on three months to a year and holding for a month or three, the ground is orange. Buying winners pays. [[0.4]] The peak is one point two two percent a month.

s3.corner.text: In the far corner, ranking on four years and holding for two, the ground is blue, and the same rule loses half a percent a month. [[0.45]] That is not a different market, or even a different theory. It is mean reversion, on the same map.

s3.tie.text: And here is the part I did not expect. [[0.45]] The two lowest points on this map are minus zero point five five, [[0.3]] and minus zero point five five. [[0.5]] Opposite corners.

s4.shape.text: That shape is not a coincidence, because I know exactly what went into this market. [[0.4]] Three things, and each owns a feature of the map.

s4.bounce.text: One. Every price carries an error that is in today's number and gone from tomorrow's. [[0.35]] Rank on a single month and that noise is most of what you are ranking on. [[0.4]] That is the notch.

s4.diffusion.text: Two. News is priced in slowly, over sixteen months here. [[0.4]] So a stock that moved on news last quarter is still moving on it now. [[0.35]] That is the ridge.

s4.overshoot.text: Three. The move overshoots, and the overshoot is handed back over years. [[0.45]] That is the basin.

s4.slice.text: Now one straight line across the map. Hold for a month, and walk the lookback out to four years.

s4.camps.text: Under water. [[0.4]] Over the ridge. [[0.4]] And back under water. [[0.55]] Momentum people stand here. Reversion people stand here. Neither is wrong.

s5.gross.text: Two things this picture is not telling you. [[0.45]] The first is that every height on it is gross.

s5.cost.text: Every rebalance trades, and the near edge trades constantly. [[0.35]] The one-month rule replaces ninety percent of what it holds, every month.

s5.sag.text: Charge ten basis points a trade on the turnover these portfolios really generate, and that edge sags. [[0.4]] The notch goes from minus fifty-five to minus ninety-two.

s5.worse.text: The second is worse. [[0.45]] I drew this map from a market whose rules never changed, and I chose them.

s5.one_path.text: You get one path, once. [[0.45]] Every height on your map has to be estimated from the stretch you have already lived. [[0.5]] The ridge is real here. Whether it is there next year, this picture cannot say.

s6.restate.text: So. [[0.55]] The same chart, two opposite bets. What decides which one is right?

s6.answer.text: Not the chart. [[0.4]] And not the market. [[0.5]] Two numbers. How far back you look, and how long you hold.

s6.same.text: It moved too far, it will come back. [[0.4]] It has been moving, it will keep moving. [[0.45]] The same sentence, at two different horizons.

s6.close.text: Which is why the horizon is not a detail of the strategy. [[0.4]] It is the strategy.
